label: verify-q2-critic

claims.claim: Published noise estimates (Kramer R2max 0.81; Landrum tau 0.51-0.71) imply a ceiling of r about 0.85-0.95, above leakage-free models on CASF2016 (r 0.75-0.80); noise is not the binding constraint there.
claims.source_says: "maximum possible squared Pearson correlation coefficient (R(2)) on large data sets is estimated to be 0.81." Landrum: Kendall tau 0.51 minimal, 0.71 maximal curation. CleanSplit: GEMS 0.803, GenScore 0.780, Pafnucy 0.746.
claims.note: The cited numbers are real, but the 0.85-0.95 ceiling is the agent's own tau-to-r conversion under normality and equal-reliability assumptions (script reproduces 0.847/0.948), and GEMS at 0.803 is just above the stated 0.75-0.80.

claims.claim: Leakage between PDBbind and CASF inflates scores: 49% of CASF complexes have near-duplicates, and a similarity-lookup gets r 0.716 with no learning.
claims.source_says: "nearly 600 such similarities were detected between PDBbind training and CASF complexes, involving 49% of all CASF complexes." Top-5 similar complexes search: Pearson R = 0.716 (0.653 on CleanSplit).
claims.note: Figures match the Graber full text; the 0.716 is for the original PDBbind split.

claims.claim: In a controlled simulation, split type changes reported r from 0.90 to 0.20 while 0.8 log-unit label noise changes it by under 0.05.
claims.source_says: sim_table.md: random_pairs noise 0.4 r=0.904; both_heldout 0.4 r=0.200; random_pairs noise 0.0 r=0.916 vs noise 0.8 r=0.871 (difference 0.045).
claims.note: Table reproduces the claim; it is the agent's own synthetic simulation with a large label SD (2.64), which the agent itself flags, so it shows mechanism only.

overall: Three key claims checked: two supported (the leakage numbers match the Graber 2025 text, and the simulation table reproduces), one partly supported (the 0.85-0.95 ceiling is the agent's own derived arithmetic, not a published figure). Sources I could fetch all opened. I did not re-run the 15-minute simulation.
